text_version.note: Full text of the EnEfG (§§ 1-21 and Anlagen 1-3), which is Article 1 of the Gesetz vom 13.11.2023 (BGBl. 2023 I Nr. 309). Articles 2-3 of that act are not part of this text; the entry-into-force date comes from the portal footnote. Standards cited (DIN EN 50600 series, ISO 50001, ISO 50005, DIN EN 17463) are not included.

summary.short: Germany's Energy Efficiency Act sets national energy-saving targets and duties for federal and Länder governments, public bodies and energy-intensive firms, and imposes PUE limits, renewable-electricity, waste-heat reuse, energy-management and annual reporting duties on data centres of 300 kW or more. In force 18 November 2023, with phased dates to 2030.
summary.long: The EnEfG sets 2030 targets for final and primary energy consumption, annual savings duties for the Federation (45 TWh) and the Länder (3 TWh) from 2024 to 2030, and 2% annual savings for public bodies using 1 GWh or more. Firms averaging more than 7.5 GWh must set up an energy or environmental management system; firms above 2.5 GWh must publish certified implementation plans for economic savings measures, avoid and reuse waste heat, and report waste-heat data for a public platform. Data centres (non-redundant connected load of 300 kW or more, network nodes excluded) must reach a PUE of 1.5 from July 2027 and 1.3 from July 2030 if operating before 1 July 2026; later centres must reach PUE 1.2 and a reused-energy share of 10%, rising to 15% and 20% for centres opening from July 2027 and July 2028, with exemptions tied to heat-network agreements. Operators must cover electricity 50% from renewables from 2024 and 100% from 2027, set up management systems by July 2025 (certified from 2026 above 1 MW), report Anlage 3 data annually to a federal register, and show customers their energy use. Administrative fines reach EUR 100,000.

territorial_scope.description: Germany (federal statute); duties of the Länder concern their own territory, and listed security, defence and nuclear bodies and facilities are excluded (§ 21).

notes: Text-internal issues, recorded as written: (1) § 20(2) No. 2 sets a first-reporting tier for data centres from 200 kW to under 500 kW, but § 3 No. 24 defines a Rechenzentrum only from 300 kW non-redundant connected load; both are coded. (2) 7.5 GWh appears twice: in § 8(1) as a firm-level trigger (Unternehmen averaging more than 7.5 GWh must set up a management system) and in § 12(4) as one of two joint conditions of a data-centre exemption from § 12(1) (consumption not above 7.5 GWh plus at least 50% of reused energy taken up via a heat network); § 12(1) applies 'Unbeschadet von § 8'. Both are coded. (3) § 19(1) No. 3 refers to '§ 9 Absatz 2 Satz 1' and § 10 and § 19(1) No. 2 refer to '§ 9 Absatz 1', but § 9 in this text has no numbered paragraphs (the confirmation duty is in § 9 sentence 4). (4) § 20(3) requires IT operators to provide 'Informationen nach § 13 Absatz 2', but § 13(2) is an ordinance authorisation and § 13(1) binds only data-centre operators; the text does not say which information IT operators provide. (5) § 11(2) No. 2 uses 'Anteil' for the 10% step and 'geplanten Anteil' for the 15% and 20% steps. (6) § 6(3) describes Directive (EU) 2018/2002 as last amended by Directive 2012/27/EU. (7) § 19(3) excludes § 19(1) No. 7 (waste heat) from BAFA's competence without naming another authority. § 19 lists no fine for § 11(5) (renewable electricity), § 12(3) and (5) sentences 2-3 (certification), § 15 or § 20(3). Left for the resolve stage: the authority for § 19(1) No. 7; content of any ordinances under § 13(2) (additional information duties) and § 18 (exemptions for climate-neutral firms from §§ 11-13 and 15-17); the European database in § 14; any amendments after the original text. Firm-level duties (Unternehmen, §§ 8, 9, 10, 16, 17) are coded with addressee 'general_public' because the vocabulary has no generic firm role; they also bind data-centre operators that meet the thresholds. Anlage 3 size classes (< 500 kW up to >= 100 MW IT load) are reporting categories and are not coded as thresholds.
